To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stimulation of muscle synthesis following ingestion of essential amino acids in young healthy men is dependent upon activation of the mammalian target of Rapamycin complex 2 signaling pathway.
the activation of mTOR complex 1 (TORC1) is required for the increase in human muscle protein synthesis following ingestion of L-essential amino acids (L-EAAs).
the activation of mammalian target of the rapamycin complex (mTORC) 1 signaling is required for the increase in muscle synthesis in response to essential amino acid ingestion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of protein synthesis in muscle, and the effects of nutritional interventions on protein synthesis in humans.
the mechanisms that regulate protein synthesis in skeletal muscle, which is important in the maintenance of muscle mass and function.
how dietary protein and amino acid intake influences muscle protein turnover in healthy young and older adults and how this process is altered in disease states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mTORC1 pathway is required for the EAA-stimulated increase in human skeletal muscle protein anabolism.
the mTORC1 signaling pathway is required for the increase in muscle-protein synthesis in response to L-essential amino acids in humans.
mTORC1 is required for muscle protein synthesis in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mTORC1 is necessary for muscle protein synthesis in humans.
mTORC1 is required for the increase in muscle anabolic signaling and muscle protein synthetic rates that occur following EAA ingestion in humans.
we have demonstrated that mTORC1 signaling is required for the increase in muscle anabolic response to EAA in young healthy men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mTORC1 pathway is required to stimulate muscle protein synthesis in humans in response to amino acid surplus.
mTOR is an important regulator of muscle protein synthesis, and this is true in both rodents and humans.
amino acid ingestion is a potent stimulant of muscle protein synthesis, but the stimulation of muscle growth requires activation of mTOR.
